The EU's Digital Product Passport requirement is reshaping how physical products carry verifiable data. AuthiChain is built to generate and anchor that data trail — from raw material sourcing to point of sale — using signed QR codes and on-chain anchoring, so a product's provenance record travels with it instead of living in a spreadsheet somewhere else.

Each unit gets a cryptographically signed QR code. Scanning it surfaces the product's passport: origin, custody events, and certifications tied to that SKU. The underlying record is anchored to a public ledger, so the passport history can't be quietly edited after the fact.

We built AuthiChain because brands preparing for the DPP rollout need infrastructure that treats provenance as a data layer, not a marketing microsite. If you're mapping your supply chain against EU DPP requirements and want to see how a signed passport works end to end, take a look.

https://authichain.com/eu-dpp?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=eu-dpp-launch&utm_content=a

reddit.title: Anyone else building for the EU Digital Product Passport requirement?
reddit.body:
I've been working on AuthiChain, a system for generating signed QR-based product passports and anchoring the provenance record each one points to, so the history can't be silently rewritten after the fact. It's aimed at brands that need to trace a product's history — origin, custody, certifications — from raw material to shelf, ahead of EU DPP requirements.

Curious how others here are approaching the technical side: building the passport layer in-house, using a vendor's DPP platform, or bolting a QR code onto an existing ERP? What's been the hardest part — the data model, the QR issuance side, or getting suppliers to actually submit clean data?

Disclosure: I work on this project.
